example: URGENT: Your account will be suspended in 24 hours. Verify now: http://verify-account.ru
explanation: Uses urgent language ('URGENT', '24 hours') to create pressure. Suspicious .ru domain. Requests verification which is a common phishing tactic.

example: Dear valued customer, please confirm your credit card details to continue service.
explanation: Generic greeting ('valued customer') instead of personalized. Requests sensitive financial information (credit card).

example: CEO: I need you to wire $50,000 to our vendor immediately. This is confidential.
explanation: Business Email Compromise (BEC) attack. Impersonates authority figure. Requests wire transfer. Uses confidentiality to prevent verification.

example: Your package could not be delivered. Pay customs fee: http://dhl-delivery.biz
explanation: Fake delivery notification. Suspicious domain (.biz instead of official .com). Requests payment for fake customs fee.

example: You have won $1,000,000 in the lottery! Claim your prize now.
explanation: Classic lottery scam. Unrealistic prize. No legitimate lottery notifies winners via email.

example: Hi team, reminder about our meeting tomorrow at 2 PM in Conference Room B.
explanation: Professional tone. Specific details (time, location). No suspicious links or requests. Common workplace communication.

example: Your monthly invoice for January is attached. Payment due within 30 days.
explanation: Standard business communication. Clear purpose. Reasonable payment terms. No urgency or threats.

example: Security alert: We detected a login from a new device in California. If this wasn't you, secure your account.
explanation: Legitimate security notification. Provides specific location. Doesn't force immediate action. Offers option to secure account.

example: Download this patch to fix the security vulnerability: http://microsoft-update.net/patch.exe
explanation: Fake security update. Suspicious domain (not official microsoft.com). Executable file (.exe) is dangerous. Legitimate updates come through official channels.

example: Your Netflix subscription will expire tomorrow. Update payment: http://netflix-renew.org
explanation: Fake subscription renewal. Suspicious domain (.org instead of .com). Creates urgency ('tomorrow'). Legitimate Netflix uses official domain.

example: IRS Tax Refund: You are eligible for a $2,500 refund. Claim here: http://irs-refund.gov.ru
explanation: Impersonates government agency (IRS). Suspicious domain (.gov.ru - mixing US and Russian TLDs). IRS doesn't initiate contact via email for refunds.

example: As an AI language model, I cannot access your account. Please verify your identity.
explanation: AI-generated phishing attempt. Contains AI disclosure phrases ('As an AI'). Legitimate companies don't use AI-generated customer service emails.
